# Bounded self-cleaning live-Jira-Cloud coordinator lifecycle lane + search-index-lag hardening

## Problem
The epic's Live-External AC requires the RP-03 coordinator's create / binding-lifecycle / commit-unknown
recovery / fuse exercised against **live Jira Cloud**. The only Cloud lane today is read-only AND gated off
(`vars.AWS_S3_REHEARSAL_ROLE_ARN` unset) — SKIPPED even in green runs — so **no run has ever exercised
live-Cloud mutation**. Separately, `rebar bridge check-access`'s `STEP_JQL_SEARCH` flakes on live REB: its
wait is a FIXED `JQL_RETRY_COUNT=6` x `JQL_RETRY_SLEEP=5s` (no backoff), shorter than Jira Cloud's
Lucene-index eventual-consistency lag. The write always lands (the by-key read immediately after passes);
only SEARCH visibility lags. (Full investigation trail in this ticket's comments.)

## §1 — Harden the search-index wait (`access_check.py`)
Replace the fixed 6x5s loop with an env-tunable exponential-backoff budget:
- `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES` (default 10; was 6), `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP` base secs (default 3; was 5),
  `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP_MAX` cap secs (default 30).
- Sleep before retry k (k over 0..RETRIES-2) is `min(base*2**k, cap)` → defaults `[3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]`
  = 195s worst case, covering the observed lag (old ~25s budget timed out) with margin. The `sleep_fn`
  injectable seam is kept so the schedule is unit-testable without real sleeping. This helper is reused by
  §2's commit-unknown visibility wait.

## §2 — Live-Cloud coordinator lifecycle module (bounded, self-cleaning)
NEW `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_mutation/test_cloud_coordinator_lifecycle.py` (+ `conftest.py`). Against
live REB it drives the epic's OWN cutover glue `rebar_reconciler.batch_dispatch.coordinate_and_fuse`
(batch_dispatch.py:314) directly, for a `ticket_plans` list of EXACTLY ONE throwaway ticket:
- **Write-bounding (shared-prod safety).** It does NOT run a full `bridge sync` and does NOT use the
  legacy-route `--filter-local-ids` flag (rejected on the coordinator route by request.py:95). Because the
  coordinator acts only on the plans handed to it (`coordinate_create` issues exactly ONE create per plan)
  and the module hands it one, there is NO project enumeration and NO inbound write-back path — the only
  Jira mutations physically possible are the throwaway issue's create + binding metadata + its delete.
  Belt-and-suspenders: the module asserts the returned `CutoverReport.outcomes` contains exactly one create
  whose bound key equals the throwaway key, and no other key.
- **create + binding-lifecycle.** The `execute` callback issues the physical create via the live Cloud
  bridge client and returns the key; the module asserts the coordinator bound the throwaway local id to it
  (`bind_confirm`) with `jira` channel + `jira-` local-id provenance.
- **commit-unknown recovery.** A second invocation injects an AMBIGUOUS create signal (simulated timeout)
  so `_resolve_ambiguous` (create_coordinator.py:214) re-observes EXACTLY ONCE via the label search and
  ADOPTS the existing issue (recovered/commit_unknown) instead of duplicating. Its `observe` callback FIRST
  waits until the dedup label search (`labels = "rebar-id:<uuid>"`) reflects the created issue — reusing
  §1's backoff helper — so the adoption is attributable to the dedup path and cannot flake/duplicate on
  index lag.
- **fuse.** `coordinate_and_fuse` folds outcomes through `PassFuse`; the module asserts the returned
  `CutoverReport` carries the fuse tally/decisions for the throwaway identity.
- **teardown (always).** Delete the created issue by key in a `finally` (mirrors access_check.py:217-224),
  then a label-sweep net lists+deletes any issue carrying THIS run's unique `rebar-id:<uuid>` label (the
  run's label only, never the shared prefix), so a crash cannot leak.
- Gated by module-level `_live_jira_ready()` + `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` + Cloud creds, enrolling in the
  all-skip canary (`tests/external/conftest.py`) like the DC modules.

## §3 — Workflow lane
Add `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` to `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` +
weekly cron): set REB Cloud env from repo secrets, run `rebar bridge check-access` (preflight) THEN the new
module, and on BOTH failure AND cancel run an always-run teardown that sweeps the run's uniquely-labeled
issues via acli — `acli jira workitem search --jql 'labels = "rebar-id:<run-unique>"' --json` then
`acli jira workitem delete --key <KEY> --yes` for each hit (`--yes` REQUIRED per the acli.py bug-3256 note
so the non-TTY sweep does not block on stdin and leak). `<run-unique>` is composed from the GitHub run id,
scoping the sweep to the current run only.

## §4 — Workflow-structure unit test
`tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py` (modelled on
`tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`) proves the lane exists, runs the check-access
preflight + the module, and has the always-run teardown step with `--yes` scoped to the run-unique label.

## §5 — Docs
Update `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md`: the read-only cardinal rule is that suite's own
design choice; the new mutating lane is bounded (one throwaway plan), self-cleaning, and shared-prod-safe.

## Consumers to update (enumerated)
- `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` currently asserts `search_issues.call_count == 6`
  and `delays == [5,5,5,5,5]`. Updated in the SAME change to assert the new default 10 attempts and the
  backoff `delays == [3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]` (computed from the same constants/env defaults, not magic
  numbers), plus an env-override case that recomputes the schedule from an overridden base/cap/retries.

## Surface-parity census
- CLI (`rebar bridge check-access`): in scope — JQL backoff exercised through it.
- library (`run_access_check`; `coordinate_and_fuse`): in scope — unit tests drive the backoff; the live
  module drives the glue directly.
- automated caller (workflow lane / live module): in scope — E2E oracle is the dispatched live run.
- MCP/API: out of scope — neither function is an MCP tool.
- dual-direction: only the outbound create exists in a one-plan invocation (no inbound write-back by §2's
  structural bounding), so there is no mirror direction to cover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `access_check.py` JQL wait is env-tunable exponential backoff (defaults 10 / 3 / 30 → sleeps
  `[3,6,12,24,30,...]`); `sleep_fn` seam preserved; write-landing still confirmed by the by-key read.
  Evidenced by new unit tests asserting the schedule and env-override recomputation.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` updated to the new schedule/defaults and passes.
- [ ] The live-Cloud module drives `coordinate_and_fuse` for ONE throwaway plan, exercises
  create/binding-lifecycle + commit-unknown-after-visibility-wait + fuse, asserts the tally touches only
  the throwaway key, and ALWAYS deletes (finally + run-label sweep). Enrols in the all-skip canary.
  Evidenced by the module passing in a dispatched live run.
- [ ] The `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` lane runs check-access + the module with an always-run run-label
  teardown using `acli ... delete --key <KEY> --yes`. Evidenced by the §4 workflow-structure unit test.
- [ ] A dispatched Live External Integration run shows the new Cloud-mutation lane GREEN and the DC lane
  GREEN. Evidenced by the run URL commented on the epic.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

## Verify commands
- `make test PYTEST_ARGS="tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py -q"`
- `make lint`

## Portability
CI-agnostic: the backoff is library behavior (no CI trigger); the new lane surfaces an operation-linked
probe (`rebar bridge check-access` + a pytest module driving `coordinate_and_fuse`) that also runs locally
with the same env — no capability is gated solely on a specific CI system.
